gljs/render-tests/terrain/heatmap: Over terrain, GL JS colors each tile's kernel density on its own and blends the tiles, so where kernels of two tiles overlap their density doesn't add up; mln-rs adds it up across tiles, as both do without terrain. The kernels stand where GL JS draws them; 1,552 of 262,144 px differ, all where kernels of the fixture's two GeoJSON tiles overlap
gljs/render-tests/terrain/occlusion-debu: P4 (standing layers): terrain draws, but doesn't occlude what stands behind it yet; its DEM source declares tileSize 256 for tiles/terrain-shading's 512 px tiles
gljs/render-tests/terrain/symbol-height-: P4-S5 (terrain hides what stands behind it): the aircraft stands on the ground and draws where GL JS draws it; 481 of 262,144 px differ, along ridges' silhouettes; its DEM source declares tileSize 256 for tiles/terrain-shading's 512 px tiles
gljs/render-tests/terrain/symbol-line: P4-S4 (line labels follow the ground): the label stands on its line on the ground, but its glyphs are spaced along it by C++'s perspective ratio, not by the one they draw at: 258 of 262,144 px differ, the label 0.6% shorter than GL JS's
